paper.title: Efficient Agent Training for Computer Use
paper.central_claim: With only 312 human computer-use trajectories augmented by Trajectory Boost (9 teacher-sampled alternative single-step actions per human step from Claude 3.7 Sonnet, 27K samples), SFT of Qwen2.5-VL-72B gives PC Agent-E, a 141% relative improvement over the base and 10% over the teacher on WindowsAgentArena-V2, more effective and efficient than human-only SFT or direct distillation, and it generalizes to OSWorld.
paper.claim_scope: Windows desktop, screenshot-only, 141-task author-modified WAA-V2 (feasible tasks only); 72B backbone; SFT; OSWorld Linux used as a cross-platform check. Also releases WAA-V2 as a secondary resource contribution.

evidence.quote: Starting with just 312 human-annotated computer use trajectories, we further augment them by synthesizing diverse alternative action decisions with Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
evidence.support_explanation: Central recipe: tiny human seed set plus teacher-synthesized alternative decisions.

evidence.quote: our PC Agent-E model achieved a remarkable 141% relative improvement, and even surpassed the Claude 3.7 Sonnet by 10% in relative terms on WindowsAgentArena-V2
evidence.support_explanation: Headline performance claim (base model and teacher comparison).

evidence.quote: we utilize a frontier computer use agent model, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, to generate single-step alternative action decisions.
evidence.support_explanation: Operation: single-step teacher sampling, not end-to-end rollouts.

evidence.quote: These sampled action decisions from Claude 3.7 Sonnet are not executed in real computer environments, but serve as important augmented data for later agent training.
evidence.support_explanation: Alternative actions are never executed or verified; no environment feedback enters the selection.

evidence.quote: In practice, we sample 9 action decisions in parallel.
evidence.support_explanation: Scaling factor s=10 (9 teacher + 1 human) per step.

evidence.quote: the history in the training sample includes only prior human actions on the main trunk of the Traj Tree
evidence.support_explanation: History visible to the student is always human-trunk history, even for teacher-sampled alternative actions.

evidence.quote: We finally obtained 27K training samples from 312 augmented trajectories
evidence.support_explanation: Training-set size actually used for SFT.

evidence.quote: we provide Claude 3.7 Sonnet with: task description, historical actions with their previously reconstructed thought processes, the current action, and the corresponding screenshot.
evidence.support_explanation: Thought Completion is hindsight reconstruction conditioned on the human action.

evidence.quote: we retained only trajectories whose task descriptions have an overlap of 0 under 13-gram and less than 0.7 under 3-gram, and a cosine semantic similarity under 0.85 with respect to any test task.
evidence.support_explanation: Decontamination rule against WAA-V2 test tasks.

evidence.quote: no additional verification was required to ensure trajectory correctness
evidence.support_explanation: Human trajectories are accepted without execution-based verification.

evidence.quote: over 90% of trajectories contain fewer than 15 steps
evidence.support_explanation: Training horizon distribution is short; authors tie 50-step degradation to it.

evidence.quote: an updated benchmark comprising 141 tasks across 11 widely-used Windows applications, all derived from the original WindowsAgentArena
evidence.support_explanation: Main evaluation benchmark is authors' modified fork of WAA.

evidence.quote: as a temporary solution in WindowsAgentArena-V2, we removed all infeasible tasks to prevent infeasible hacking
evidence.support_explanation: Benchmark modification: infeasible tasks dropped.

evidence.quote: We implemented VM snapshot restoration before each evaluation
evidence.support_explanation: Resettable-environment control added to WAA-V2.

evidence.quote: This approach reduced the initialization failure rate from 10%–30% (depending on hardware) to below 5%.
evidence.support_explanation: Initial-state validation with up to three restarts.

evidence.quote: We identified and corrected several evaluation errors and relied on human evaluators for a few complex tasks to improve assessment reliability.
evidence.support_explanation: Checker fixes and partial human evaluation; counts of fixed checkers / human-judged tasks not given.

evidence.quote: Compared to training on human trajectories alone, which yields a limited gain (improved from 14.9 to 17.2), PC Agent-E achieves substantially greater performance gains (improved from 14.9 to 36.0).
evidence.support_explanation: Human-only SFT vs Trajectory Boost ablation (s=1 vs s=10).

evidence.support_explanation: Direct-distillation baseline definition.

evidence.quote: The resulting 3,120 trajectories are then used for training with the identical procedure as PC Agent-E, matching the trajectory number of our method for a fair comparison.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline matched on trajectory count, not on step count or on filtering.

The text describes no success filtering, verifier or rejection sampling of the 3,120 distilled teacher trajectories, whose source model succeeds on only ~33% of tasks (E018); the baseline therefore appears to train on unfiltered, partly failed trajectories. signatures.object: SFT training set for a screenshot-only ReAct policy (thought+action per step, history = text log of earlier human thoughts/actions)
signatures.information: Teacher (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, non-thinking, in PC Agent-E scaffold) sees <task, screenshot o_k, human-trunk history h_k> at each recorded human step; no later frames, no execution; student never sees teacher history, only human-trunk history.
signatures.operation: At every human step, sample 9 single-step (thought, action) alternatives from the teacher in parallel; keep human step as the 10th; each node becomes one SFT sample (Traj Tree).
signatures.output: 27K SFT samples from 312 trajectories; Qwen2.5-VL-72B SFT 2 epochs.
signatures.conditions: Needs a seed set of correct human trajectories with recorded screenshots; teacher must be strong at single-step decisions; states restricted to human-visited trunk.
signatures.feedback: None from the environment; alternative actions are not executed.
signatures.selection_rule_data: No filter/verifier/majority vote on teacher actions is described; selection of the whole recipe against baselines is done on the WAA-V2 test tasks (the benchmark the authors built).
signatures.persistence: Student weights after SFT; no memory/skill store.
signatures.later_use: Single-pass evaluation on WAA-V2 (30 steps) and OSWorld (30 steps).
signatures.claimed_effect: 14.9 -> 36.0 on WAA-V2 (E019, E017); >teacher 32.6 (E018); beats human-only 17.2 and direct distillation 26.2/26.9 (E022, E026).
signatures.failure_boundary: Termination awareness collapses beyond training length (50 steps, E036-E037); 7B gain small (5.0->6.4, E030-E031); knowledge/grounding not improved (E029); wrong teacher actions are not detectable.

signatures.object: Per-step thought text of human trajectories
signatures.information: Claude sees task, earlier reconstructed thoughts, the current human action (and click-marked screenshot) and writes a first-person pre-action thought (hindsight with the action visible).
signatures.operation: Iteratively reconstruct a thought for each human action; then use (thought, action) as SFT target.
signatures.conditions: Action-conditioned (so thoughts are action-consistent by construction).
signatures.selection_rule_data: none described (no check that reconstructed thought would lead to the action without seeing it)
signatures.later_use: student produces thought then action at inference
signatures.claimed_effect: Part of the human-only baseline (17.2); no separate ablation of thought completion.
signatures.failure_boundary: Hindsight leakage and rationalization risk not examined.

signatures.information: Authors inspect original WAA and identify (i) no VM reset between tasks, (ii) FAIL-always hack on infeasible tasks, (iii) unstable initial states, (iv) buggy checkers.
signatures.operation: VM snapshot restore per task; remove all infeasible tasks; initial-state validation with <=3 restarts; fix some evaluation functions and human-grade a few tasks -> 141 tasks.
signatures.conditions: Evaluated tasks are only those with feasible goals.
signatures.feedback: The weaker base model scores higher on infeasible tasks in WAA and OSWorld (E034, E032-E033).
signatures.selection_rule_data: Authors choose what to drop/fix after assessing the original benchmark; selection was made before final results (not stated).
signatures.claimed_effect: More robust and fair evaluation; initialization failure 10-30% -> <5% (E015).
signatures.failure_boundary: Evaluator corrections not enumerated or two-sidedly validated; dropping infeasible tasks removes refusal ability from measurement; benchmark and method are from the same group.

retention_trace.reason: component_training claim: no retained-improvement or self-improvement loop is claimed. The chain is recorded as a static recipe.

chain.proposed_change: SFT on 312 human trajectories with thoughts + 9 teacher single-step alternatives per step (E003-E007)
chain.selection_data_rule: no accept/reject of teacher actions; recipe compared against baselines on the same test benchmark (E022, E026)

gap.author_gap: Open-source computer-use agents lag proprietary systems; the key factor is scarcity of high-quality trajectory data (E045).
gap.checked_gap: Real: desktop/Windows trajectory data is expensive to collect; end-to-end teacher rollouts need online VM interaction (reported 900 h for 3,120 trajectories, E027). The fixed neighbors address web tutorials (AgentTrek) or large VM infra with multi-stage filtering (UI-TARS); neither targets a tiny human seed set on Windows. The paper never compares against AgentTrek/UI-TARS-style data at equal budget; the delta is argued in related work only (E046).

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: tutorial-guided replay with VLM evaluator filter; $0.55 per trajectory, web-focused
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: not Windows desktop; filters on outcome, not human-anchored states

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: iterative online trace bootstrapping with rule/VLM/human filtering and reflection tuning at VM scale
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: needs hundreds of VMs and annotators; a 312-trajectory regime is not considered

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: teacher rollouts need no human seed

gap.residue: Teacher knowledge about planning/recovery is not yet in open student; human trajectories alone (17.2) do not transfer it; whether teacher single-step signals at human states are accurate is unmeasured.
gap.stakes: Data-efficiency of open Windows agents (312 trajectories vs ~900 GPU-hours of rollouts).
gap.method_response: Anchor on human-visited states (cheap, always valid), ask the teacher only for single-step decisions offline, train on the multiplicity of decisions; avoid long-horizon error accumulation (E047, asserted).
gap.remaining_gap: Alt actions unverified; no filtered-distillation or best-of-N teacher control; termination weakness; gains stay in planning, not grounding/knowledge; small-model gain minimal; same-group benchmark; no repeats.
gap.unresolved: Whether Trajectory Boost beats a success-filtered distillation baseline of the same teacher; contribution of human-state anchoring vs sample multiplicity (Fig 7 not readable in text).
gap.current_relevance: Later UI-TARS-2 (fixed ref 2509.02544) reports 50.6 on WindowsAgentArena; not used to judge this paper's problem placement.

claims.text: PC Agent-E gets 141% relative improvement over Qwen2.5-VL-72B on WAA-V2.
claims.setting: Windows VM, screenshot-only, 30 steps, 141 feasible tasks, 72B
claims.selection_vs_test: Benchmark built by the authors; training tasks decontaminated against it (E009); no separate dev split described
claims.result_denominator: 14.9 -> 36.0 over 141 tasks; non-integer rates (E021); no repeats (E042)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Large gain on this author benchmark for a single reported training run; magnitude uncertain without repeats.

claims.text: PC Agent-E surpasses its teacher Claude 3.7 Sonnet by 10% relative.
claims.result_denominator: 36.0 vs 32.6 (3.4 pts, ~5 tasks of 141) and vs 35.4 (0.6 pts)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Student is comparable to the teacher (and to the thinking teacher); 'surpasses' is not statistically established.

claims.text: Trajectory Boost is more effective and efficient than human-only SFT and direct distillation.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Beats unfiltered teacher-rollout distillation at equal trajectory count and is far cheaper in wall-clock; superiority over success-filtered distillation or equal-step controls is untested.

claims.text: Gains come from improved planning (verification and self-correction).
The method generalizes to OSWorld (34% relative improvement).
claims.setting: OSWorld 369 tasks, 30 steps, trained on Windows data only
claims.selection_vs_test: OSWorld not used in training; decontamination not stated
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small but real feasible-task gain on a different OS; absolute level low; infeasible score confounds the headline.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the authors' feasible-only WAA-V2, SFT of Qwen2.5-VL-72B on 312 human trajectories plus 9 unverified teacher alternatives per step raises success from 14.9 to 36.0 and beats unfiltered Claude end-to-end distillation at the same trajectory count; a smaller feasible-task gain (4.4 -> 10.9) appears on OSWorld.
unresolved: no repeats or CI; non-integer table values unexplained
attribution between human-state anchoring, teacher thoughts and sample multiplicity
WAA-V2 is a same-group modified benchmark
assessment.reproduction_note: All numbers are author-reported; nothing was re-run.
assessment.evidence_level_note: 'transfer' rests only on the OSWorld Linux online gain (platform unseen in training); if the grader requires decontamination or repeated runs on the transfer set, it would be online.

G.reason: Real bottleneck (scarce desktop trajectories; costly rollouts) and a clear delta statement, but nearest neighbors (AgentTrek, UI-TARS, OS-Genesis) are discussed only in related work, no equal-budget comparison, and the residual (what AgentTrek-style data cannot do on Windows) is not shown.

M.reason: Operation is concrete and reproducible (human trunk + 9 single-step teacher samples, history from trunk only) and yields a testable prediction versus direct distillation (error accumulation avoided), which is tested by DD baselines. Weakened by no validation/filter of teacher actions, no explanation why the student exceeds the teacher, and mechanism claims resting on 50 anecdotal trajectories.

X.reason: Prompts, action space, training sample structure, hyper-parameters and scaffold-training correspondence are given; failure boundaries (50 steps, 7B) are stated. Missing: selection/quality gate for synthetic actions, termination supervision, treatment of image history.

E.measurement.reason: Online execution-based checkers on 141 tasks with VM reset, but checkers were edited by the authors with no two-sided error measurement, a few tasks human-graded without counts, the benchmark is own-built, and table values are non-integer fractions of task counts without explanation.

E.causality.reason: Human-only (17.2), DD (26.2), human+DD (26.9) and scaling-factor controls give real attribution to teacher decisions on human states; but no filtered-DD, no same-step or same-compute control, no ablation of Thought Completion or of state anchoring, mechanism by 50-trajectory reading.

E.holdout.reason: Task-text decontamination against the test set is explicit (n-gram + semantic) and OSWorld offers a second OS, but apps/environments overlap with training by design, the test benchmark was designed by the authors after seeing the failure modes, and OSWorld decontamination is not stated.

E.statistics.reason: No seeds, repeats or confidence intervals; differences against the teacher are 3.4 points (about 5 tasks) and 0.6 vs thinking Claude; failure analysis is qualitative over 50 trajectories; 7B and OSWorld are single entries.

E.cost.reason: Reports annotation effort (2 people, 1 day), training compute (32 GPUs, ~5 h), synthesis wall-clock (3 h vs 900 h) and step-budget sensitivity; teacher token/API cost and per-model interface differences (UI-TARS gets image history) are not accounted for.

status.reason: Full html text (v2) read including all appendices; figure-only numbers (Fig 3/7/8) are not in the text but do not block scoring because the table and prose carry the key results.

rationale.summary: PC Agent-E is a data-efficiency training recipe: keep 312 human trajectories as trusted states, ask Claude 3.7 Sonnet offline for 9 alternative single-step decisions per state and SFT Qwen2.5-VL-72B on the 27K resulting samples. Reported online results (14.9 -> 36.0 on the authors' feasible-only WAA-V2; 11.1 -> 14.9 on OSWorld) are large against the base model and against unfiltered end-to-end distillation, and the 300x cheaper generation is a real practical point.
strengths: Clear, reproducible operation with prompts and training structure
Several relevant controls (human-only, DD, human+DD, scaling factor)
Explicit decontamination rule and cost reporting
Honest limitation analysis of the 50-step regression and 7B result
weaknesses: Teacher actions are never executed or filtered; no filtered-distillation or compute-matched baseline
No repeats/CI; 'surpasses teacher' is a 3.4-point (0.6 vs thinking) margin on 141 tasks; non-integer table entries unexplained
WAA-V2 is the authors' own modified benchmark, with infeasible tasks dropped and checker fixes not enumerated
Mechanism (planning gain) shown by 50 anecdotal trajectories; Thought Completion not ablated
